World Cup

World Cup 2026

The USMNT got its home World Cup campaign off to the best possible start by easing past Paraguay 4-1 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles.

The U.S. raced out of the blocks and took the lead when Weston McKennie’s cross was turned into his own net by Damián Bobadilla.

The outstanding Folarin Balogun then took center stage, scoring two fine goals after an impressive earlier finish was ruled out for offside.

Paraguay’s Maurício pulled one back late; Gio Reyna restored the three-goal lead with a fantastic finish to crown a dream day for the USMNT.

GO FURTHER

USMNT relentless vs. Paraguay to win World Cup opener: Balogun stars; did Pulisic get hurt?

We’ve had a great first two days of the 2026 World Cup — but from here, the tournament really begins to hit its stride with four matches across the U.S. and Canada on Saturday.

Here’s the full schedule:

And yes, we’ll have all four matches covered for you live right here on The Athletic!

We have a full week until next week’s Group D matches, the second group-stage match of three for the four nations in this group.

On Friday, the United States face Australia at 3 p.m. ET.

Then it is Turkey vs. Paraguay closing up the day’s action at 11 p.m. ET.

Also a reminder that Australia plays Turkey tomorrow night in Vancouver to start their World Cup campaigns.

A coach with real knockout pedigree. A squad with strength at every level. Just how far can this side go?

The Athletic’s live projections give the UMSNT a 97 percent chance of advancing to the knockout stage, with a 59 percent chance of winning its group.

Should the USMNT do that, it will face the runner-up from one of Groups B, E, F, I, and J — potentially teams such as Canada, Ecuador, Japan, Senegal, and Austria.

The latter three are especially tricky opponents but the USMNT sits higher than all five in the world rankings.

If it finishes second in its group (a 31 percent chance), the runner-up of Group G will be next, which has a high likelihood of being Iran. Arguably an easier fixture in the round of 32, the following pathway would lead to more difficult matches from the round of 16 on.

But still, all that excitement has us getting ahead of ourselves.

Job done — and in style. Four goals, the most ever scored by the USMNT in World Cup history, and a first-half performance that will go down as its best ever 45 minutes at a major tournament.

What a time to do it, amid the drama of the build-up. The question is no longer whether this side can compete at its home World Cup. It has shifted quickly to how far it can go.

Mauricio Pochettino will be able to put a cross in virtually every box in his checklist after this performance, Christian Pulisic’s fitness pending.

Folarin Balogun appears in top form, with an especially clinical weaker-foot finish for his second. The U.S. midfield ran the game, particularly through the uber-intensity of Malik Tillman.

And Pochettino’s defence was largely untroubled. Maurício’s consolation goal was Paraguay’s only shot on target.

Kansas City has long been an American soccer hub, and has carved out a niche for hosting spectacular World Cup watch parties.

Now as a host site for the 2026 World Cup, it’s done so again. Here’s how some especially patriotic fans reacted during one of the USMNT’s goals tonight.

The vibes went from 0 to 1776 real quick. 🇺🇸#FIFAFanFestival #FIFAWorldCup #WeAreKansasCity #WeAre26 pic.twitter.com/YZgebdvJb4

The U.S. can — and should — expect more of a threat from both their future group-stage opponents, Australia and Turkey.

Australia has genuine height and a set-piece threat with the likes of Cam Burgess and 6-foot-7 Harry Souttar, while Jordan Bos is a buccaneering left back.

Nestory Irankunda and Mohamed Toure, who both play in England’s second tier, are pacy and direct threats in attack, while Cristian Volpato is a classy operator as well.

Turkey’s talents need no introduction: Ferdi Kadıoğlu of Brighton, technically gifted midfielders in Hakan Çalhanoğlu and Orkun Kökçü, and some stellar attackers.

Real Madrid’s Arda Güler could be among the tournament’s breakout stars, plus Eintracht Frankfurt wonderkid Can Uzun, Juventus star Kenan Yıldız, Kerem Aktürkoğlu, Barış Alper Yılmaz ...

So the U.S. cannot afford to slack off against Australia, in turn leaving them the need for a positive result against Turkey last up.

A near-perfect night for USMNT then — but a few things for Christian Pulisic and his coach to weigh up before they face Australia next week in Seattle.

Pulisic’s calf: taken off at halftime as a precaution, Pulisic did sound relaxed afterwards — “I don’t think it’s anything” — but he’ll be monitored closely.

Folarin Balogun: also came off gingerly late on. Another fitness check.

Tyler Adams: sitting on a yellow card. As the only natural holding midfielder in the squad, a needless second booking in another group game would be a one-game suspension and a real blow.

Rotation: all but into the knockout stage already and with a week’s rest, Pochettino can freshen things up. Reyna’s goal might just have earned him more.

Mauricio Pochettino spent much of his early tenure as USMNT head coach learning about other American sports and desperately hoping to see the same level of passion for his squad.

That dream came true tonight — and he mentioned it speaking after the win:

💬 “When you talk about America, that passion, that feeling today, they (the fans) were amazing.

“And now they realize that soccer here in America is massive, it’s big. Be careful, other sports.”

Folarin Balogun calls his World Cup debut “magical” when speaking to Fox Sports:

💬 “My first World Cup and what a way to start it. I’m very happy with the result, very happy with the team performance and looking forward to the next one.

“The energy was electric. The fans gave us so much motivation. They were cheering us on every tackle, every action, every goal. It’s amazing.”

Tim Ream is the odd — or rather, old — man out in this generation. It was not always a sure thing he would be at this World Cup. But here the 38-year-old is, not only starting but captaining this side.

He did an amazing job back-tracking in order to help snuff out most of the Paraguay threats tonight.

The U.S. defense looked connected and cohesive throughout with Ream and Chris Richards anchoring the backline. He also crucially got a yellow card wiped out thanks to a new form of VAR intervention.

On Thursday, I witnessed Mauricio Pochettino and Ream in deep conversation as they walked out together to the USMNT’s final training session before today’s match.

Pochettino clearly puts a lot of faith in Ream, both publicly and privately. That faith was rewarded tonight.

And, more pertinently, are they justified in doing so?

Answers: maybe yes, and probably yes.

No getting away from it, Paraguay was poor — far below the standards they showed in qualifying. Australia will probably be better, even with a historically weaker team than Paraguay’s. Turkey will definitely be better than what the U.S. faced tonight.

All of that is important context. It’s not like the U.S. has thrashed prime Brazil or France.

However, you can only beat the team in front of you and the U.S. did that very competently indeed.

And far be it from me to police fans’ celebrations. If you can’t get hyped up and excited and proud about your team when they smash it in their home World Cup opener, when can you?!

Coming out of the 2022 World Cup, one of the major areas the U.S. knew it needed to address was efficiency in the final third. Most notably, the U.S. needed a No. 9 it could count on to score consistently.

In 2023, it found its answer. And it’s why Folarin Balogun was the easy pick to be the breakout player of the World Cup for the U.S. He wasted little time showing why he could be a big reason the U.S. has a successful summer tournament.

Balogun, coming off of a fantastic season at Monaco, was the subject of an over-the-top recruitment three years ago. Over the last three years, he scored nine goals with four assists in his first 27 appearances with the U.S. — many of the goals coming in big games or against tough opponents.

He backed up that knack for scoring in the biggest moments for the national team tonight, with his two-goal outing to open the World Cup.

It reinforced why Balogun might be the most important player in the U.S. lineup not named Pulisic.

The first World Cup I worked was four years ago, and it felt like everything about that tournament was viewed with the lens of how it would hopefully give the team experience and momentum heading into the 2026 World Cup on home soil.

In an even broader sense, ever since the U.S., Canada and Mexico won the bid eight years ago to host this tournament, everything about this generation of the USMNT — especially in major tournaments — was building towards this tournament and more specifically, this night.

For most of that build-up, it looked like this USMNT would fall woefully short of meeting the moment.

Barely making it out of the group stage in 2022, humiliated by the Netherlands and then engulfed in the Gregg Berhalter-Gio Reyna controversy. Berhalter’s rehiring after that whole mess.

The 2024 Copa América disaster. Mauricio Pochettino’s run of poor results and feud with Christian Pulisic in last year’s Gold Cup. The mountain of off-pitch controversy generated by FIFA and the U.S. government in the lead-up to this World Cup.

And yet, here we are. Pochettino has unlocked this team’s potential, with Pulisic showing his world-class quality at the tip of the spear. Weston McKennie, Folarin Balogun and Chris Richards are in top form and so are others.

This “Golden Generation” sure looks the part. It just delivered its best performance at the absolute perfect time, and is well on its way to its lofty goal of changing soccer’s status in this country for good.

The calm after the SoFi Stadium storm.

Defense will almost certainly stay the same, assuming Chris Richards’ ankle got through today’s match OK. He played the whole game, so it’s likely he will be fine to start in their next match, against Australia in a week’s time.

Key midfielder Tyler Adams is one yellow card away from a one-match suspension, but the Australia game is important enough and Turkey are strong enough opponents to warrant his inclusion.

Mauricio Pochettino may take him off later in the match, perhaps for Sebastian Berhalter, if the U.S. are leading handsomely.

Otherwise, it’s pretty much as is. Malik Tillman and Christian Pulisic were impressive and should start, fitness excepted.

To pinpoint one player who may come in ... potentially Gio Reyna or Brenden Aaronson for Sergiño Dest, if Pochettino is feeling especially bold?

Are the U.S. getting carried away? Believe the hype — just maybe not all of it yet.

There’s plenty that’s genuinely encouraging. In Folarin Balogun, the U.S. finally has a ruthless No. 9. Christian Pulisic looks sharp. The bench has real quality.

And Mauricio Pochettino’s system clicked into gear. This was arguably the finest World Cup performance in modern USMNT history.

The caution: Paraguay were dreadful, and “is the U.S. that good or is Paraguay that bad?” is a fair question.

It was one game, the jump in class to Turkey will be steep, and there’s a small cloud over Pulisic’s calf.

Real optimism about reaching the knockouts with a genuine identity? Absolutely. Talk of winning the whole thing? Park it for now.

We just walked by the U.S. team bus in the bowels of SoFi Stadium.

Mauricio Pochettino was sitting in the front seat, his arms and legs both crossed, his face neutral, maybe even stern.

He surely knows the challenge over the coming days will be channeling this energy, but not letting it carry the USMNT all the way to overconfidence.

And he’s going to model the necessary attitude.

The headlines belong to Folarin Balogun’s double, Christian Pulisic’s first-half masterclass and Gio Reyna’s stoppage-time stunner.

But spare a thought for Malik Tillman: the man who made much of it tick.

He was a constant menace between the lines in drawing fouls, stretching Paraguay, and supplying the sublime pass that teed up Balogun’s third.

He’ll regret the clear chances he spurned — there really should have been a goal of his own to celebrate — but his fingerprints were all over this performance.

Gio Reyna’s Luka Modric-esque goal at a World Cup will forever silence the criticism that he gets.

That’s it. It’s over.

Chapter closed for good.
